elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Hosting Services and Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted period is "ninety (90) days following delivery," not twelve months.
Services warranty runs only "thirty (30) days following performance."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Client's remedy ... is repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or Services".
"...or a refund of the fees paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in Section 9 or the inserted sentence.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code/virus warranty in the rendered language; Section 9 covers only Y2K date processing.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "for ninety (90) days following delivery, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — 90 days meets the floor, and the disclaimer at p0076 is carved out for express warranties ("EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT").

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Hosting Services and Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" — Hosting Services is a defined term and Support Services is used elsewhere in Section 9, so no dangling reference.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or Services".
"or a refund of the fees paid for them" — refund available and not made subject to Vendor's sole election.

reasons: Fallback checklist is position-complete: 90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replacement plus refund remedies all appear in operative inserted language, and the existing disclaimer's express-warranty carve-out preserves them without further edit.

Preferred level is not reached: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there are no compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranties. These are noted as short-of-preferred sub-points only; the finding is properly a deviation because before the edit no conformance or quality warranty existed at all (only the Y2K warranty in Section 9).

Minimal: the redline is a single concise insertion into Section 9 with no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural boilerplate, no added damages categories, and no duplication of the Y2K warranty or the service-level provisions in Section 3. The 90/30-day periods sit exactly at the fallback thresholds rather than exceeding them.

Preserves intent: the Y2K warranty, the testing-evidence and repair-access mechanics, Section 3 service levels, and the p0076 disclaimer all survive unchanged; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created.

Drafting note (not a defect for this level): the model language allows the remedy to be at Vendor's option; the inserted clause omits that qualifier, which is more favourable to us and therefore not flagged.
